newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate down 40 bps to 11.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate down 40 bps to 11.3 pct.

text.p: ZAGREB, Jan 22 ( Reuter) - The Croatian average lending rate dropped 40 basis points to 11.3 percent on Wednesday in lively trade and amid an abundant supply of kuna funds, dealers said.

They estimated total daily trade at 57.2 million kuna, up from Tuesday's 17.2 million and leaving a surplus of 32.7 million on the supply side. Demand for another 4.7 million kuna loans was not met as borrowers and lenders failed to agree on terms.
Fresh borrowings accounted for 43.5 million kuna, most of which were granted at a steady call money rate of 11 percent.
Rates for term loans ranged from 12 percent for one-week to 16 percent for one-month loans.
Insurers rolled over previous loans at 10 percent.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Thursday weaker at 5.8641 against the dollar and 3.5636 against the mark. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
